Its sound comes from the vibration of the body, and it carries the rhythm of Gnawa music; it belongs to the culture of the Maghreb in North Africa and is associated with Algeria, Morocco, Libya and Tunisia. A Gnawa ensemble usually has one sintir and may have up to twenty krakeb players; in the Gnawa style the two plates stay closed between strokes, giving mainly the impact sound, while in Tunisia they are opened quickly so that the ring is more audible.

卡爾卡巴鐵響板主要作為甘納瓦音樂的節奏部分，屬於北非馬格里布聲音景觀。甘納瓦音樂: The qraqeb carry the rhythm of Gnawa music above all, part of the sound world of the Maghreb in North Africa. Gnawa music stands for the history of sub-Saharan West Africans sold as slaves in what are now Algeria, Morocco, Libya and Tunisia; in the culture its sound is tied to horses' hooves, grain sacks and shackles, and it also stands for the shackles taken off when a slave was freed. The origin of the name is unknown, and this sense does not appear in standard Arabic. In playing, the Gnawa style keeps the plates closed between strokes, while the Tunisian style opens them quickly after the stroke; the ensemble usually has one sintir and as many as twenty qraqeb players.
卡爾卡巴鐵響板主要出現在格納瓦音樂的節奏部分，屬於北非與馬格里布聲音文化的一環。: The qraqeb carry the rhythm in Gnawa music above all, part of the sound culture of North Africa and the Maghreb. In a Gnawa ensemble one sintir is usually joined by up to twenty players, who strike hand-held iron clappers again and again to hold the rhythm. The Tunisian way differs from the usual Gnawa style: the plates are opened quickly after the stroke so that the ring is clearer, while elsewhere they are mostly kept closed and struck, bringing out a short impact sound.
卡爾卡巴鐵響板屬體鳴樂器，發聲來自器身振動。來源記載其以鐵或鋼手工製成，外形近似: The qraqeb is an idiophone, its sound coming from the vibration of the body. Sources record that it is made by hand from iron or steel and looks like a large iron clapper; the body is four cymbal-like sounding pieces, two on each side, joined by rope. The player holds one set in each hand and strikes the metal pieces against each other. Beyond iron, steel and rope, sources do not state the materials of other parts, nor the surface treatment or the materials of the fittings.
卡爾卡巴鐵響板為體鳴樂器，發聲來自器身振動。演奏者通常一手持一副，每副由繩索串連: The qraqeb is an idiophone, its sound coming from the vibration of the body. The player usually holds one set in each hand, each set made of four cymbals threaded on a rope, two on the left and two on the right. The basic action is to strike both hands at once; in the Gnawa style the plates stay closed after each stroke, bringing out the clap, and in the Tunisian style they open quickly after the stroke, bringing out the ring. To begin, practise a firm grip and steady repeated strokes, then fit your rhythm to a single sintir and several other players.
卡爾卡巴鐵響板音色明亮尖銳，具有鮮明的金屬質感。其音域位於高頻區域，能夠穿透樂隊: The qraqeb have a bright, sharp timbre with a clear metallic quality. They sit in the high frequencies, cut through the other parts of an ensemble and mark the pulse plainly. The clack of iron on iron is dry and carries, and the resonance is short, with no long tail. Beside the hand cymbals of Western percussion the qraqeb sound sharper and more abrasive, more aggressive in colour; beside a marimba they have none of its warm resonance, showing instead the cold hardness of metal. Their particular clatter gives Gnawa music its strong North African flavour and is an indispensable part of the ensemble's rhythmic foundation.
